transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-17 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Lucas Patel (Redwood SE), Riley Gomez (Redwood CSM) -- Anika Rao (Sable Head of ML), Diego Martín (Infra Lead), Priya Singh (Legal), Owen Brooks (Product)

Auto-summary (may be rough): quick renewal/expansion sync. customer wants Azure East as main region, wants committed capacity bump, legal has a few KMS and audit asks, SE to run perf in Az East with their sample set.

00:00 Maya: okay good morning/afternoon everyone thanks for joining, I think we have 50 minutes on the calendar, we'll run through renewals, region plan for Azure East and then open q's.
00:12 Anika: yeah thanks Maya, um quick context, we've been happy with Redwood latency but as we scale to more personalized models we need both predictable cost and an extra region closer to our east coast users.
00:24 Maya: got it. high level ask is committed cap increase and new region?
00:29 Owen: yes, committed capacity +40% and bring Az East online as primary for east coast — that will shift about 35% of traffic there.
00:39 Lucas: quick clarifier — when you say Az East, do you mean Azure East US (eastus) or East-US-2? sometimes infra teams use different naming.
00:47 Diego: eastus 2 ideally, for redundancy to our existing services. we also want dedicated instances not shared host, because of PCI-ish workloads.
00:58 Maya: okay dedicated Reserved / Redwood Dedicated makes sense. pricing wise we can model a committed discount for 12 months vs month-to-month. we'll share a worksheet.
01:10 Priya: legal question up front, do you support customer-managed KMS and HSM? Also need audit logs retained for 12 months and SAML SSO with SCIM provisioning.
01:22 Riley: yes on KMS integration we have a private deployment option with KMS/HSM integration — I can pull the SOC2 + architecture notes after the call. audit logs available, retention can be configured, but we'll confirm the retention windows.
01:36 Anika: and performance — we saw a few spikes last quarter, want to make sure your autoscaling and burst capacity will handle our peak for payments flows.
01:46 Lucas: absolutely. two things: autoscale + burst pools on Dedicated can be configured, and we also suggest KV prefix caching for conversational flows. we'll propose a batching and cache configuration to balance latency and cost.
01:58 Diego: what's the realistic p95 latency for gen requests at our target qps? we were seeing mid 200s on average in our test env.
02:08 Lucas: early estimate for Az East dedicated nodes, with quantized model and continuous batching tuned, p95 should be around 120-180ms for the model you're running — but we need to run with your prompt distribution to be precise.
02:22 Anika: okay we'll send the sample request distribution and token histograms.
02:27 Owen: timeline wise procurement expects renewal signed by end of May if possible.
02:32 Maya: we can aim for that — I'll get the pricing and SOW draft to you by 5/20.
02:36 Priya: legal needs to review but procurement timeline is realistic, we'll need redlined SOWs at least a few days.
02:43 Anika: can we also get a canary rollout plan for Az East? we don't want traffic cut-over to cause regressions.
02:50 Lucas: yes, we'll propose a canary with progressive ramp and automatic fallback to the prior region/model variant — Redwood supports routing policies and automatic fallback to a compatible variant if capacity constrained.
03:03 Diego: how does the KV cache behave across regions? we don't want long cold-start penalties.
03:09 Lucas: good point — prefix KV cache is per-region; warmup can be mitigated by slow ramp or pre-warming typical sessions. we can also replicate hot keys if you need cross-region consistency but that's an advanced setup.
03:24 Anika: any impacts to cost for replication?
03:27 Lucas: yes, replication increases network and storage overhead — we'll quantify in the proposal but generally it's an incremental cost vs improved latency.
03:34 Owen: about billing — do you support invoicing to our purchasing team and monthly usage reconciliation?
03:40 Maya: yes, we can do monthly invoices for committed reservations and overage billing. also support billing contacts and PO-based invoicing.
03:48 Priya: on data residency and encryption, we need confirmation that customer data at rest in Az East will be under our KMS keys and logs only stored in that region.
03:58 Riley: we'll confirm the regional retention and KMS scoping. we do support customer-managed keys for private deployments; for hosted endpoints we need to review the SOW for specifics — I'll follow up with the deployment option matrix.
04:14 Anika: also wanted to confirm RTO/RPO during failover for Az East to our primary region — we need <5 min failover for user-facing flows.
04:23 Lucas: our recommended pattern is active-passive with warm standby in the alternate region; failover tempo can be sub-5 minutes with the automated routing policies, assuming warmed cache and pre-provisioned nodes. we'll document the playbook.
04:36 Diego: ok that's acceptable as long as we test it in the benchmark.
04:40 Lucas: we'll include a failover stress test in the perf run.
04:45 Maya: next steps recap — I'll send pricing and SOW by Thursday (5/20). Lucas will schedule the perf benchmark in Az East, recommend a 2-hour window next week. Priya will send legal must-haves for SOW redlines.
04:57 Priya: yes I'll share a short list, probably 3-4 clauses to look at.
05:02 Anika: last question — competitors: we've looked at BigCloud AI and ModelServeX and Redwood's performance is favorable but cost differential matters. can you put a note on cost assumptions in the worksheet?
05:13 Maya: yes we'll include modeled cost comparison assumptions and include latency/cost tradeoffs for quantization and batch configs.
05:20 Owen: can we get a one-pager of the canary runbook for our ops team?
05:24 Riley: yes, I'll attach a canary runbook and the recommended rollback triggers.
05:29 Diego: okay great.
05:31 Maya: awesome thanks everyone, we'll follow up in writing and lock in the benchmark time.
05:36 Anika: thanks, talk soon.
